subject: FH-520 won't start after winter
body:
Good evening, and I hope this finds you well. I run a small hobby farm with a few goats, some chickens, and an orchard that my late father planted, and over the years I have collected a fair number of tools and machines that I only use now and then. This year, my neighbor, who is also my oldest friend, finally talked me into getting rid of the old stumps along the fence line. I bought an FH-520 stump grinder in the fall (order FE-109871), used it for two afternoons, and then put it away in the barn for the winter after the first hard frost.

I went to start it this week and the engine will not start at all. It cranks, or tries to, but nothing catches. I did not add any fuel stabilizer before storing it, and I think the gas may be to blame. Could you tell me what I should do to get it going again, whether I need to drain the tank or replace anything, and whether there is a service step I should have done before storage? Thank you kindly.

Bernard Oyler

subject: Log kicked off splitter
body: Hello, I am writing because last weekend while using my FH-210, a piece of log flew off the splitter wedge and struck me on the leg. I am bruised but otherwise fine. I would like to understand what went wrong. I was splitting a fairly dry round of ash, standing at the side. Was I doing something incorrectly, or could there be a problem with the machine? I would appreciate your guidance before I use it again. Thank you.

Is it regular business hours, weekdays only? And is there a direct line, or do I go through a main number? Our crew is in the field most mornings so I'd probably call around two in the afternoon. If there's a better method like email I'm happy to do that instead, whatever is easiest for you. Thanks! Darlene Whitaker, Whitaker Lawn & Landscape.

subject: Hose fitting failure, FH-P90
body:
To whom it may concern:

I am writing regarding my FH-P90 pressure washer, which I use around my small hobby farm for cleaning equipment and animal pens. Last Thursday, while I was rinsing a tractor implement, a high-pressure hose fitting burst from the pump outlet and the spray caught my nephew's hand, which required a bandage but no further treatment. I have since moved the machine into the barn and have not used it again.

My concern is the cause of the failure. The washer was purchased in March and has been used perhaps a dozen times. The hose and fitting appear to be the original components, and I did not alter them in any way. I would like to know whether this is a known issue with the fitting, what replacement part I should order, and whether you require the broken fitting to be returned for inspection. I can supply photographs and the order number, FE-117902, upon request.

Sincerely,
Harold Weatherby

subject: 340 pallet damage
body:
Howdy! We got our pallet of FH-340 chippers in and the driver didn't hang around for us to check them. Two have bent hoppers, one has a busted guard. Nobody signed for anything as far as I know since I was out on the lot. Can you point me to who handles freight damage? Thanks, appreciate y'all.

Buck Tolliver, Tolliver Farm & Ranch Supply

subject: Splitter ram stuck
body:
Good morning from Vermont. I hope you are well. Let me explain my situation a bit. I retired from teaching shop class in the spring and my wife and I bought a lot with a lot of old maples, and my plan has been to heat the place with wood this winter. My son-in-law told me about your company and I bought the FH-210 in August. I've had my share of trouble in life with small engines, so I wasn't worried. The first month went great.

Now the thing is, the ram goes forward on a split and then will not come back. The pump just whines the whole time I hold the lever. I am quite frustrated, because I have about nine cords sitting there and the temperature is dropping. I am a patient man but I am running out of time. Can you tell me what is likely wrong and whether I can fix it myself or need to send it in? Serial FH210-24-01733.

My wife says to also tell you the machine is a handsome piece of equipment, for whatever that's worth.

subject: Maintenance question
body: I just want to make sure I'm looking after my FH-210 right. How often do I change the engine oil, and what about the hydraulic fluid? Anything I should do with the wedge? And what's the right way to store it for the winter? I'm out on the farm most days so a quick list works fine. Thanks.

subject: no power from FH-G7 outlets
body:
I bought an FH-G7 for my dad's house and I'm so frustrated. The engine runs fine, sounds great, but when we plug anything into the outlets nothing works. Not the work light, not a fan, nothing. Once, the breaker on the front popped when we tried the freezer. Dad has been without backup power for a week because of this and I'm the one who told him to buy it. I need to know what is wrong and whether it's the outlets or the breaker or something else, and what I can do to fix it. Order number FE-120455.

Also, a quick question: where do I buy spare parts, like a replacement breaker, if it comes to that?

subject: Blade set for the FH-340 I gave my dad

I've also called twice and just got a voicemail loop. I'm trying to be a good kid here, but this is a little frustrating. Can you point me to the right blade set and tell me how to order? His serial is FH340-23-04419 and the order was under my name, FE-102906. Please reply by email.

subject: Bad batch of FH-340
body:
Good afternoon,

This has been a strange month at Whitlow Grounds & Gardens. We started the season with a crew shortage, and then our truck needed a new transmission, which set us back a good ten days. My brother-in-law has been helping on weekends, and he keeps joking that we should have gone into accounting. Anyway, the spring cleanup contracts for the three apartment complexes are finally back on track, which is a relief, since we nearly lost the largest one. We have been loyal buyers of your equipment for years and we resell a few units to the smaller outfits that work with us.

On to the actual point of my message. We received a shipment of FH-340 chippers last week and four of the six have cracked welds along the feed hopper, and a couple more have bolts that do not seem to match the frame. I would like to know how to report this properly and how you would like us to handle those units. I have photos. Please let me know who to send them to. Thanks again for your patience with a rambling email!

Warm regards,
Derek Whitlow
Operations Manager, Whitlow Grounds & Gardens

subject: Damaged pallet, delivery of FH-G7 generators
body:
To Whom It May Concern:

On Tuesday, a freight carrier delivered a pallet of portable generators, model FH-G7, to our store. The driver departed before we could inspect the units, and the delivery receipt was not signed by our staff. Upon unwrapping the pallet, we found visible crush damage to the frames of at least two units. We wish to document the damage and understand how to proceed with a freight claim. Photographs are available upon request. Please advise on the correct procedure.

Sincerely,
Helen Marchetti
Owner, Marchetti Hardware & Supply

subject: Order FE-139902 discrepancy
